purpose: External evidence for the load-bearing structural assumptions in the AI-compute worked example. Distinct from parity_ledger.json (which records only the v2.5->v0.1 translation). Each entry states the claim, the basis class, and the source. Basis classes: verified (checked against a cited primary/secondary source), industry-reported (widely reported, not independently verified here), assumption (analyst judgement, not a sourced fact). This example is illustrative; entries marked industry-reported or assumption should be re-checked before any external use.
as_of: reflects sources cited in the project record; market-share figures are time-sensitive and should be re-verified

methodology_citations.claim: Critical-node detection in sparse graphs is an established problem.
methodology_citations.source: Arulselvan, Commander, Elefteriadou, Pardalos (2009), 'Detecting critical nodes in sparse graphs', Computers & Operations Research 36(7):2193-2200.

methodology_citations.claim: Supply-chain disruption modelling via network/OR methods is established.
methodology_citations.source: Snyder et al. (2016), 'OR/MS models for supply chain disruptions: A review', IIE Transactions 48(2):89-109.

methodology_citations.claim: Microelectronics supply-chain lock-in and substitutability is an active analytic topic.
methodology_citations.source: UVA National Security Data & Policy Institute (2025), 'Microelectronics Supply Chain Analysis: Lock-In and Substitutability.'

structural_assumptions.claim: ASML is the sole manufacturer of EUV lithography machines.
structural_assumptions.used_for: asml_euv has no alternative in any requirement group -> frontier-persistent.
structural_assumptions.source: ZEISS, 'High-NA EUV lithography', states ASML is the only manufacturer of EUV lithography machines: https://www.zeiss.com/semiconductor-manufacturing-technology/inspiring-technology/high-na-euv-lithography.html (market status is time-sensitive; re-verify before external use).

structural_assumptions.claim: ZEISS is the exclusive supplier of the optical systems for ASML's EUV machines.
structural_assumptions.source: ZEISS, 'High-NA EUV lithography', documents ZEISS as the exclusive optics partner for ASML EUV: https://www.zeiss.com/semiconductor-manufacturing-technology/inspiring-technology/high-na-euv-lithography.html

structural_assumptions.claim: TRUMPF supplies the high-power CO2 drive laser for EUV light sources, and is the exclusive supplier of it.
structural_assumptions.used_for: asml_euv 'source' group = {trumpf_source} with no alternative (exclusivity is what makes it frontier-persistent, not merely its role).
structural_assumptions.source: TRUMPF/ZEISS/Fraunhofer fact sheet '5 facts about EUV lithography' documents TRUMPF as the exclusive supplier of the EUV drive laser: https://www.trumpf.com/filestorage/TRUMPF_Master/Corporate/Press/Press_releases/2020_21/Corporate/20201125-PR-TRUMPF-ZEISS-FRAUNHOFER-DZP/Fact_sheet_5_facts_about_EUV_lithography_EN.pdf ; role also at https://www.trumpf.com/en_US/solutions/applications/euv-lithography/euv-drive-laser/

structural_assumptions.claim: Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) is used in high-performance IC substrates with a dominant market position.
structural_assumptions.used_for: cowos 'substrate' group = {abf_substrate} with no alternative; drives ABF frontier-persistence on the stack.
structural_assumptions.source: Ajinomoto R&D, bioscience & fine chemicals, documents ABF's role and market position in high-performance semiconductor substrates: https://www.ajinomoto.com/innovation/rd-organizations-and-facilities/bioscience_chemicals/technology (share figures are time-sensitive; re-verify).

structural_assumptions.claim: CoWoS (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate) is TSMC's advanced 2.5D packaging platform, and the frontier stack routes advanced logic through it.
structural_assumptions.used_for: stack waypoint sequence includes cowos between fab and server.
structural_assumptions.no_concentration_claim: This entry asserts role only. It does NOT claim CoWoS is sole-source: alternative OSAT 2.5D capacity exists and IS modelled (osat_ase/osat_amkor paths). CoWoS's frontier-persistence in results comes from the stack routing choice, not from an unstated monopoly assumption.
structural_assumptions.source: TSMC 3DFabric documents CoWoS as TSMC's 2.5D advanced-packaging platform: https://3dfabric.tsmc.com/english/dedicatedFoundry/technology/3DFabric.htm

structural_assumptions.claim: Polished silicon wafers are a required input to every advanced fab.
structural_assumptions.concentration_claim: The wafer sector is concentrated among a few producers (Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, Siltronic, SK Siltron).
structural_assumptions.used_for: every fab AND_DEPS includes wafers:{si_wafers}; removing wafers disables all fabs on the stack.
structural_assumptions.source: Role verified: SUMCO CSR Report 2024 documents SUMCO as a major silicon-wafer producer supplying advanced fabs: https://www.sumcosi.com/english/csr/pdf/csr_rep24en.pdf . Concentration (few-producer market structure) is industry-reported, not established by this single-producer source; specific shares are time-sensitive. The node aggregates multiple producers, so its flat-critical status is a resolution artifact (see PARITY caveat).

structural_assumptions.claim: SMIC operates mature nodes without EUV (export-controlled) and serves a domestic design ecosystem.
structural_assumptions.used_for: smic_mature has no euv group and design:{china_design}; provides the topological (non-frontier) route.
structural_assumptions.source: SMIC EUV export-control status and domestic focus, widely reported. Re-verify current node capability.

structural_assumptions.claim: Germanium feeds optical/photonic components (transceivers, fiber), not the sub-5nm logic path.
structural_assumptions.used_for: germanium edges go to optical_xcvr/fiber_optic only -> zero frontier impact.
structural_assumptions.source: Analyst judgement on germanium's role in this graph's resolution; defensible but not independently sourced here.

structural_assumptions.claim: EUV/advanced photoresists are a required fab input, and JSR is a leading EUV-photoresist supplier.
structural_assumptions.concentration_claim: Advanced photoresist supply is concentrated in a few Japan-heavy suppliers (JSR, TOK, Shin-Etsu, Fujifilm).
structural_assumptions.used_for: photoresists is an any_of member of every fab's 'resist' AND group -> removing it disables all fabs -> frontier-persistent. fluorochemistry (an upstream input to photoresists) is modeled as non-cascading (see note).
structural_assumptions.source: Role verified: JSR documents its EUV photoresist role and leadership: https://www.jsr.co.jp/jsr_e/news/2022/20220802.html . Concentration (few-supplier, Japan-heavy market structure and specific shares) is industry-reported, not established by this single-supplier source, and is time-sensitive. The node aggregates multiple suppliers, so its category-level criticality is a resolution artifact. Re-verify before authoritative use.

structural_assumptions.claim: High-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI accelerators is supplied by SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron; it is a required input to advanced 2.5D packaging.
structural_assumptions.used_for: cowos 'hbm' group = {sk_hynix_hbm, samsung_hbm, micron_hbm} (OR within the group); modeled as multi-supplier so no single HBM vendor is frontier-critical.
structural_assumptions.source: HBM three-supplier structure, widely reported. Re-verify current share and qualification status.

structural_assumptions.claim: Advanced accelerators are integrated by ODM/OEM server assemblers and served through hyperscale clouds; multiple assemblers and clouds exist.
structural_assumptions.used_for: server nodes (foxconn/quanta/wistron/supermicro/dell_hpe) and cloud nodes (aws/azure/gcp/oracle) are the stack's server and cloud waypoint groups; modeled as multi-provider OR so individual assemblers/clouds are not frontier-critical.
structural_assumptions.source: Multi-vendor server ODM and hyperscale cloud structure, widely reported. Azure/GCP show minor topology impact only where they uniquely route a specific sink at strict; see results.json.

modeling_notes.detail: copper_foil (-> cowos/osat) and fluorochemistry (-> photoresists) are strict v2.5 edges but v2.5 does NOT cascade them (both report 0/0/0 on every v2.5 metric). They are not rendered as v0.1 dependencies, because any rendered dependency in the frozen engine also imposes a liveness cascade, which would fabricate criticality. Their downstream targets stay reachable via other rendered paths. The dropped edges are logged 'unsupported' in parity_ledger.json. This is a v0.1 expressiveness limitation (no connectivity-only relation), not a v2.5 disagreement.

activation_time_assumptions.claim: Substitutability thresholds strict/degraded/loose correspond to ~0-3 / ~12 / ~24 months and map to activation times 0/12/24.
activation_time_assumptions.source: v2.5 analyst parameterisation. The specific month values are judgement, not sourced facts; the qualitative ordering is the load-bearing part.

activation_time_assumptions.claim: Leading-edge design re-qualification onto a second foundry (e.g. Nvidia->Samsung) is a degraded (~12 month) substitution, not drop-in.
activation_time_assumptions.source: v2.5 analyst judgement. This single threshold choice governs whether TSMC is frontier-declining vs frontier-flat; flagged as the model's most consequential assumption.
